field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The inshore fishing remained good for rock fish up the coast. The anglers caught a great mix of bigger rock fish in the deep water. The halibut has been hit and miss due to the south swell. There were a few sea bass caught near Capitola. The anglers in the deep water near 5 Mile caught some bonito. The wind was down and the swell dropped today.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 3, 2026 Cool Water, Rain Spark Klamath Salmon Push Eureka resident Michael Marcelli with a nice king salmon taken earlier this week on the lower Klamath. Water conditions, as well as fishing, should be good through the holiday weekend. Photo courtesy of Alan’s Guide Service Following some excellent salmon fishing in the Klamath estuary over the past few weeks, adult fall-run king salmon are now beginning to make their way upriver. There are a couple of reasons for the push. First, cool water releases from behind Lewiston Dam began last Friday to help reduce the risk of disease in the salmon. The other factor is the weather. Cooler outside temperatures, along with a fair amount of rain, can do wonders for river temperatures. Combined, these conditions should produce a steady stream of kings moving upriver and staging in the various holes throughout the lower river. But don’t give up on the estuary just yet—the fishing was reportedly pretty wide-open on Monday. I think it’s safe to say we’re smackdab in the middle of what could be a pretty good run of kings. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: Another great day out on the water as our three salmon boats out today (Sunrise-Triumph-Tacklebuster) all limited early on the salmon for the 2nd day in a row. Great fishing out there. The bottom fishing was also really good with limits once again on the rockfish and we saw some pretty impressive Lingcod and Canary rockfish on the filet tables. One boat reported 2-crabs around for his boat.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: SNB did not run as the crew was fishing the ITC tournament on other boats. Pretty much everyone did well today, 30-40 fish, and big ones. It looks like the anchovies finally got big enough and the tuna are back on top. The fish are finally inside the 125 line. Time to make up for some spotty early fishing. ​Mike C Skunked. Ouch. Thank god the wind is going to turn over the water.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in consultation with the Pacific Fishery Management Council (PFMC), the States of Oregon and California, and advisory body members met today and have taken the following in-season management actions related to the commercial ocean troll salmon seasons from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, Oregon: ACTION TAKEN: • Effective 12:01 AM Thursday September 10, 2026, the landing limit in the ocean commercial troll salmon fishery in the area from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain is reduced to 50 coho per vessel per week (Thursday through Wednesday). RATIONALE: The current estimates are that approximately 50% of the 7,000 coho quota remains available. The reduction in the landing limit was made to facilitate continued access to the coho while also ensuring that the quota is not exceeded. There are no changes to the weekly limit of 100 Chinook per vessel. It is recommended that fishery participants that have not done so, should deliver prior to the start of the upcoming landing week beginning on Thursday, September 10 to avoid being in possession of coho in excess of revised landing limit and to allow full landing limits in the September 10th to 16th
